issues.reason: The quantity-to-strength rule puts a bare generic at strength 0.9 ("≈most") and reserves 1.0 for "all"/"every", so strength 1.0 asserts that EVERY wart is benign — more than a "generally" hedged generic states.

Same rule: an unquantified generic property of a kind is strength 0.9, and 1.0 over-asserts that every wart is contagious (the Degree atom records "slightly" and does not license raising the strength).

gaps_confirmed: adverbial generic hedges ("generally", "typically", "usually", "often") — the quantity-to-strength table lists only determiner-like quantifiers, and the QuantifierPhrase companion is licensed only when a quantifier word is present, so the hedge itself cannot be recorded
new_gaps: Degree's entity slot with a KIND filler — (Degree wart contagious slightly) puts a kind where every example shows an individual, and no rule says whether a kind-level degree modifier is licensed or must ride a distributing rule
repair_summary: Lowered (Inheritance wart benign) and (Inheritance wart contagious) from strength 1.0 to the bare-generic strength 0.9, confidences unchanged.
notes: The infection genus at 1.0 0.99, the distribution of the coordinated adjectives instead of a compound, and "slightly" kept as a surface lemma in Degree are all correct. "generally" leaves no atom of its own, since no companion is licensed for an adverbial hedge.
